question:
The chart below shows the number of men and women in further education in Britain in three periods and whether they were studying full-time or part-time.
Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
essay:
The graph illustrates the numbers of males and females enrolled in higher education in the UK in three separate periods between 1970 and 1991. The figures are divided into two categories: full time education and part-time education.

Overall, it can be clearly seen that part-time education is significantly more popular than full-time studies. While the number of female students enrolled in both modes of education and the male full-time enrolments increased over the period, the figure for male part-time students fluctuated.

In 1970, 1000,000 male students enrolled in part-time education, and the number fell to around 850000 in 1980/81, before recovering at nearly 900000 in 1990/1991. On the other hand, male full-time enrolments rose steadily, reaching a peak at slightly more than 200000.

Female part-time enrolments saw an unprecedented peak at fewer than 1100000 in 1990/1991, rising from over 700000 in 1970/71. Similarly, the figure for female full-time students had a sharp rise from 1970/71 to 1980/81, before stabilizing until 1990/1991.
